relationships.deletion_semantics: Deleting the book workspace deletes metadata unless cleanup is pending.

Deleting the book workspace first cancels active Tomato download/summary work, then deletes chapters unless cleanup is pending. Chapter files may come from import/manual archive or deterministic canonization of human-confirmed chapter_draft.md sections.
Deleting the book workspace deletes knowledge files unless cleanup is pending.
Deleted with the book workspace after active Tomato import work for that book_id is cancelled.
Deleting the book workspace deletes ignored .loregit prose delivery state. Confirm/archive success or rollback clears the active state for the resolved draft.
Deleted with the book workspace.
Marker may outlive the locked directory until cleanup succeeds.

Book deletion and successful fresh/rebuild import clear dev_repo conversation indexes and logs for the same book_id before the workspace is exposed again; failed or collision-blocked imports leave them intact.
Conversation delete removes the selected JSONL log and updates the index.
Deleting a Dify app invalidates the route until env/API key is rebound.
Deleting a book workspace deletes the files; changing route ownership, moving initialization ownership, or changing constraint lifecycle/applicability semantics requires ER/data-model amendment.

Deleting a book workspace deletes the files; changing outline write ownership, adding/removing outline targets, changing SOURCE_FACT/AUTHOR_PROPOSAL/WORLD_MODEL_REQUIRED semantics, or allowing outline to treat historical/retired/disabled world constraints as current-active requires ER/data-model amendment.

Deleting a book workspace deletes chapter_draft.md if materialized; changing continuation write ownership, length-gate semantics, or current-active constraint consumption semantics requires ER/data-model amendment.
Deleting a book workspace deletes error_archive.md if materialized; changing review write ownership or allowing review to write chapter_draft.md requires ER/data-model amendment.
Rolling runtime artifacts may outlive the live book state as repository evidence; deleting a book does not rewrite committed case-study docs.

The derived pending-review cursor, continuation workbench projection, and any style advisory, metric delta, or constraint lifecycle reference is invalidated if the underlying outline, draft, world/status/domain, or style diagnostics source artifacts are deleted or rewritten. Accepted cursor state comes from ChapterFile artifacts, not unconfirmed draft headings.

Accepted chapter_draft.md sections become formal chapters/*.md only after human confirmation. Canonization preserves accepted text and must fail rather than overwrite conflicting existing chapter files.

Style advisory summaries and metric deltas are derived evidence for continuation repair or author revision. Deleting or changing a Dify workflow invalidates future repair prompts but does not rewrite historical deltas.

Chapter context packs are derived evidence for continuation repair. Deleting or changing source outline/world/status/style/advisory/gate artifacts invalidates future packs but does not rewrite historical evidence. Packs must preserve world/status constraint lifecycle so historical-only, retired, disabled, inherited-residue, or unresolved constraints are not promoted to current-active facts.
Historical Dify run rows are controlled by Dify retention; rolling reports keep run ids as evidence.
Rolling review packets are derived evidence. Deleting a Dify route invalidates future bridge calls but does not rewrite historical packets or human decisions.
Rolling evidence records draft/sandbox commit ids but does not replace Git history.
Deleting or rolling back the draft branch invalidates the active prose delivery state. A changed draft_commit makes older review reports stale before archive or rewrite actions can proceed.
Deleting or replacing chapter_draft.md invalidates parsed chapter spans and review findings. The state must not replace the draft file as the prose source.
Structured review findings may be distilled into error_archive.md for reuse, but deleting or editing error_archive.md must not by itself change current pass/problem/archive eligibility.
Historical rolling evidence may outlive the active prose delivery state. The rolling layer may observe handoff state but must not approve, rewrite, or archive prose directly.
Deleting the draft branch removes pending review state. Deleting or renaming the source plot branch invalidates confirm until metadata is rebound or the branch is restored.

Workflow definitions do not own summary.md first-create/rebuild or initial world/status creation; post-init writes occur through Flask/LoreGit tools and per-book Git. World workflow updates must preserve constraint lifecycle and applicability scope, and post-confirm status/world maintenance belongs to the world route. Outline workflow writes may include production proposals, but proposed durable world-rule changes remain WORLD_MODEL_REQUIRED until accepted by the world-model layer. Continuation workflow writes may materialize chapter_draft.md only, may consume style metric deltas as repair guidance, and must keep unresolved or non-current-active constraints out of canon prose. Legacy reading archive workflow rows remain historical evidence only.

summary.md is invalidated when source chapters are deleted, fully replaced, or extended by accepted continuation canonization. Future first-create/rebuild and post-confirm archive refresh are owned by the backend summary archive pipeline; historical Dify-generated summary.md files remain valid book history. New backend output is rendered only after structured batch validation proves chapter coverage and required sections.

status_card.md projection is invalidated when post-confirm summary.md refresh succeeds for a newer accepted chapter range. The projection must read the fresh summary tail and fail or report a retryable derived-step error instead of silently projecting from stale summary evidence.
The route exposes the backend initialization endpoint; per-book files remain owned by BookWorkspace and GitRepositoryState.
Historical Dify rows are controlled by Dify retention/DB operations.
Historical Dify rows are controlled by Dify retention/DB operations.
Derived observation disappears when evidence query is not rerun.
Missing plugin package can break otherwise restored workflow DB rows.
Missing provider or schema breaks Dify tool nodes.
Architecture truth is versioned; runtime contract references should remain readable.

Structured world facts are intermediate derived validation data. Deleting or rebuilding source summary/world/status files invalidates future projections but does not create a new persisted source entity.
